description: The vanilla-JS dashboard served from public/ and the remaining supporting artifacts (.env.example, sample alert-rules JSON, ecosystem.config.js, README.md), plus the final end-to-end verification and cleanup. Depends on FEAT-004 (REST API, WS protocol, auth) being in place. Grounded in design.md 'Dashboard', 'Deliverables mapping', the REST/WS surface, the config table (.env.example must document every var), the alert-rule schema (sample config), and requirements AC21-AC22.
steps: public/index.html: loads ES modules via <script type="module">, references Chart.js via CDN with graceful degradation, and contains the top bar (global connectivity / PM2-unreachable banner + maintenance-mode toggle) and mount points for the overview and detail views.
public/css/styles.css: dashboard styling incl status color classes (green online, red errored, grey stopped, amber launching/stopping) and the confirm-dialog + banner styles.
public/js/api.js: REST client that reads auth from sessionStorage and attaches X-API-Key (or Authorization) to every call; maps the {error:{code,message}} envelope to thrown errors.

public/js/ws.js: WebSocket client opening new WebSocket(url, ["apikey."+KEY]) (KEY = api key, or base64 user:pass in basic mode), with backoff reconnect and re-sending subscriptions on reconnect; dispatches hello/state/process:transition/log/alert/pm2/pong.

public/js/app.js: bootstrap — read/prompt for auth into sessionStorage, open the WS, route between overview and detail views, render the PM2-unreachable banner from the pm2 message and a maintenance toggle hitting POST /api/maintenance.

public/js/views/overview.js: responsive grid of process cards (name, color-coded status, pid, CPU%, memory, uptime, restarts, mode x instances) with start/stop/restart/reload/delete buttons; stop/restart/delete open a confirm dialog before issuing the call (AC9/AC14).

public/js/views/detail.js: per-process metadata, a CPU/memory history chart via Chart.js reading /api/processes/:name/metrics with graceful degradation to a numeric table if the CDN is blocked, and the per-process error list from /api/errors.

public/js/views/logs.js: live log viewer subscribing via WS log:subscribe, a scrolling buffer with client-side text search and a level toggle (info/error only), and an initial backfill from GET /api/processes/:name/logs.

.env.example: document EVERY env var in the design config table with a short comment and a sane default/example (no real secrets): PORT, HOST, AUTH_MODE, API_KEY, BASIC_USER, BASIC_PASS, SMTP_HOST/PORT/SECURE/USER/PASS, MAIL_FROM, MAIL_TO, TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL, ALERT_RULES_FILE, METRICS_RETENTION_MIN, METRICS_SAMPLE_SEC, ERROR_BUFFER_SIZE, ERROR_LOG_APPEND, DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SEC, INTENTIONAL_ACTION_GRACE_MS, ALLOWED_SCRIPT_ROOT, DIGEST_ENABLED, DIGEST_HOUR, LOG_LEVEL.

config/alert-rules.example.json: a valid sample {rules:[...]} covering several condition types (errored, restart-threshold, cpu-threshold, mem-threshold, error-spike) with per-channel toggles and cooldowns — must validate against loadAlertRules.
ecosystem.config.js: a PM2 ecosystem file that runs dist/index.js (name pm2-monitor, script dist/index.js, env block referencing the documented vars).

README.md: what it does; install; configuration of EVERY env var; how to run in dev (npm run dev) and under PM2 (pm2 start ecosystem.config.js); full REST API endpoint reference (the design's table); example Teams MessageCard and email alert payloads; the WS protocol summary; dashboard description; and the documented limitations (whole-history log search out of scope, duplicate process names collapse to one aggregate so use unique names, maintenance mode cleared on restart since state is in-memory, instances:"max" unsupported in v1 => use an ecosystem file, per-process HTTP health checks backlogged).

Final verification + cleanup: npm install, npm run build (zero strict errors), npm test (all pass), and the boot-without-PM2 smoke (node dist/index.js with pm2 absent -> GET / returns dashboard HTML, GET /api/system/health returns JSON pm2Connected:false, process stays up). Validate ecosystem.config.js loads (node -e require) and the sample rules parse + validate. Remove any temp/test artifacts. Confirm .gitignore keeps .env/node_modules/dist/logs out. Do NOT git add . — if committing, stage only the specific intended files; leaving the work uncommitted for review is acceptable.
acceptance_criteria: GET / returns the dashboard HTML and the referenced JS modules load; the dashboard shows process cards (or an empty state) and the PM2-unreachable banner while PM2 is down.
npm install, npm run build (zero tsc strict errors), and npm test all succeed end-to-end.
Boot-without-PM2 smoke passes: process stays up, GET / returns HTML, GET /api/system/health returns JSON pm2Connected:false.

.env.example documents every env var the app reads; config/alert-rules.example.json validates against loadAlertRules; ecosystem.config.js loads; README.md has all required sections and example Teams/email payloads.
.gitignore prevents .env/node_modules/dist/logs from being staged; no secrets are committed and no temp/test artifacts remain.
verification: Run: npm install && npm run build && npm test  — all succeed.

Boot check: node dist/index.js with pm2 absent and a minimal apikey .env; curl -s localhost:$PORT/ returns the dashboard HTML and curl -s localhost:$PORT/api/system/health returns JSON pm2Connected:false; stop the process.
Run: node -e "require('./ecosystem.config.js')" (loads) and a tsx check that config/alert-rules.example.json passes loadAlertRules.
findings: Delivered the vanilla-JS dashboard under public/ (index.html with top bar, PM2-unreachable banner, maintenance toggle, confirm modal, Chart.js CDN with graceful degradation; css/styles.css with status color classes green=online/red=errored/grey=stopped/amber=launching-stopping plus banner+modal styles; js/api.js REST client reading auth from sessionStorage and attaching X-API-Key or Authorization: Basic, mapping the {error:{code,message}} envelope to a thrown ApiError; js/ws.js opening new WebSocket(url,["apikey."+KEY]) — KEY = api key or base64(user:pass) — with capped backoff+jitter reconnect and re-sending subscriptions, dispatching hello/state/process:transition/log/alert/pm2/pong; js/app.js bootstrap prompting for auth into sessionStorage, opening the WS, routing overview<->detail, rendering the pm2 banner and driving POST /api/maintenance; views/overview.js responsive card grid with control buttons and a confirm dialog on stop/restart/delete; views/detail.js metadata + Chart.js CPU/mem chart that degrades to a numeric table when window.Chart is absent + per-process error list from /api/errors; views/logs.js live WS log:subscribe viewer with client-side search and info/error toggle plus GET /logs backfill). Added .env.example documenting every env var in the design config table; config/alert-rules.example.json with 6 rules covering errored, unexpected-stop, restart-threshold, cpu-threshold, mem-threshold, error-spike (validates against loadAlertRules); README.md with what-it-does, install, full env-var config table, dev + PM2 run instructions, auth rule, complete REST endpoint reference, WS protocol summary, dashboard description, example Teams MessageCard and email payloads, error capture/export, and the documented limitations. DECISION: the ecosystem file is ecosystem.config.cjs (not .js) because package.json has "type":"module"; under ESM, `require('./ecosystem.config.js')` silently yields an empty object on Node 20.19 (module.exports is a no-op in an ESM-parsed file), so PM2 would load an empty config. The .cjs extension forces CommonJS so module.exports works; README and the in-file comment reference .cjs. Verification: npm install OK; npm run build zero strict errors; npm test 156/156 pass; boot-without-PM2 smoke (PORT=3998/3999, apikey .env via env vars) — process stays up, GET / returns dashboard HTML, GET /api/system/health returns pm2Connected:false, /js/app.js served; node -e require('./ecosystem.config.cjs') loads with apps[0].name=pm2-monitor, script=dist/index.js; a tsx script confirmed config/alert-rules.example.json passes loadAlertRules (temp .verify-rules.ts removed). No temp artifacts remain. .gitignore confirmed ignoring .env, node_modules/, dist/, logs/ (and logs/errors.log). PM2 was NOT started.
